title: Required Deposit by Payment Method and Contract Content
content:
# Required Deposit by Payment Method and Contract Content

Window Replacement Contracts — how the required booking deposit of a contract not yet released is figured, by how the contract is paid and what it carries.

**Rule.** For a contract paid by Ridgeline financing and not yet released to the factory, and only for such a contract, the required deposit is the series financed deposit percentage of the measured contract value, with no minimum, and nothing where that percentage is zero; a financed contract already released stays under the booking deposit terms. A contract paid by cash, check or card that carries exterior color, laminated glass or oversize surcharge lines requires the deposit percentage of the measured contract value plus, for the special-order lines (exterior color and laminated glass) and for the oversize surcharge lines, their upfront share of the part of those lines the percentage leaves uncovered, the sum rounded to the cent and never more than the measured contract value. Any other contract requires the standard required deposit.

The part of a group of lines the percentage leaves uncovered is the amount of those lines times one less the deposit percentage. No deposit minimum enters the special-order and oversize case.

| Payment method | Exterior color, laminated glass or oversize surcharge lines | Required deposit |
|---|---|---|
| Ridgeline financing | Any | Series financed deposit percentage of the measured contract value; no minimum; nothing at 0% |
| Cash, check or card | At least one | Deposit percentage of the measured value, plus each group's upfront share of its uncovered part; rounded once; capped at the measured value |
| Cash, check or card | None | The standard required deposit |

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs, cash, check or card)

Measured contract value $10,000; deposit percentage 25%; an exterior color line of $1,000 and no laminated glass line; oversize surcharge lines of $500; upfront shares taken hypothetically as 0.6 for the special-order lines and 0.4 for the oversize lines. The required deposit is $2,500 (25% of $10,000), plus 0.6 times $750 (the $1,000 line less 25% of it), that is $450, plus 0.4 times $375, that is $150: $3,100.00 in all.

Financed example (hypothetical): a financed percentage of 12% on a measured value of $10,000 gives $1,200.00.
